transcript.text: We replaced our old condenser dryer with a heat pump one about a month ago and honestly it's driving me mad, a normal load of towels takes nearly 3 and a half hours, the old one did it in about 90 minutes. It also feels barely warm for the first half hour when I open the door to check. Surely that's not right? Is it faulty?

It is very likely not faulty. Heat-pump dryers work like a fridge in reverse: they recover heat to dry clothes at lower temperatures (usually around 45-50°C) rather than blasting them with hot air. This makes the drum feel only 'warm' or 'barely warm', and it naturally takes longer—often double the time of an old condenser dryer—to achieve a dry result. However, to rule out simple issues, please check that your lint filter and the condenser unit (usually behind a flap at the bottom front) are completely clean, as blockages can severely reduce efficiency. Also, ensure you aren't accidentally running a 'Cool Air' or 'Delicates' programme which uses little to no heat.
[Helpful to see: image "Where the condenser and water tank are" — On a condenser dryer the water container pulls out at the top and the condenser/heat exchanger sits behind a flap at the bottom front — slide it out and rinse it. Condenser/heat-pump dryers only; layout may differ.]

Right ok, I clean the fluff filters after every load and I did the other filter behind the flap about two weeks ago, it looked clean. I'm using Cotton Cupboard Dry with a full load, so not a delicates or cool one. Does it really take that much longer though? Mine's in the garage if that matters.

Yes, it absolutely does take longer. Because heat-pump dryers use lower temperatures to save energy (around 45-50°C rather than the high heat of older models), they simply need more time to evaporate moisture from thick items like towels. A cycle taking between 2 and 3.5 hours is very typical for a full load of towels on these machines. However, since yours is in the garage, cold ambient temperatures can sometimes make the unit work even harder or slower as it tries to heat up initially. To be sure your specific model isn't running an unusually long programme by default, could you tell me the make and model number? It’s usually on a sticker inside the door opening.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
It's a Bosch, model WTH85223GB, I've got it from the receipt. Is that long time normal for that one then? I do keep opening the door to check on it, if that matters.

Yes, that is completely normal for the Bosch WTH85223GB. Because it is a heat-pump model, it dries at a lower temperature (around 45-50°C) to save energy and protect fabrics, which inherently takes longer than your old condenser dryer—a cycle time of up to 3.5 hours for thick towels is standard. The reason it feels 'barely warm' initially is because the drum never gets hot like an older machine; it builds heat gradually using a refrigeration cycle. Additionally, every time you open the door to check on the load, you let out that accumulated warmth and moisture, which resets the drying process and adds significantly to the total time.
